title: Make and Do
intro: Make and do are very common verbs in English, and they are easy to mix up. Let’s look at when to use each one.

sections.heading: Use MAKE to create something
sections.text: We use make when we produce, build or create something new.

sections.heading: Use DO for actions and tasks
sections.text: We use do for jobs, tasks, activities and general actions.
examples: What do you do for a living?

tip: Not sure which one to choose? Ask yourself: am I creating something new (make) or doing a task or activity (do)?
